text:
Claude Code tip: before you ship a vibe-coded site, have Opus 5.5 send out 𝟱 𝘀𝘂𝗯𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 to check 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘀𝗲 𝟮𝟬 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴𝘀, then fix them all in one pass:

Consistent design
→ Write a DESIGN.md first, and make every color, font size, spacing and corner radius follow it
→ Keep the palette restrained and the type hierarchy clear
→ Make every button, card and input of the same kind look alike
→ Too flat? Add emphasis. Too crowded? Cut
→ Keep text readable on both dark and light backgrounds

On mobile
→ No sideways scrolling, and nothing spilling off the screen
→ Add a mobile menu
→ Make buttons big enough to tap
→ Keep the layout intact when the text is enlarged

Every state
→ Give loading, empty and error states a proper screen
→ Give every button feedback, with its own hover, pressed and disabled look
→ Show form errors right where they happen, plus submitting, success and failure messages
→ Add transitions to modals, dropdowns and tab switches

Use it like a real user
→ Click through the core flows, like sign-up and checkout, from start to finish
→ Find buttons that do nothing and links that are broken
→ Make sure the whole thing works with just a keyboard

Before launch
→ Say what you do in one line on the home page
→ Give each page one main button you want people to click
→ Give every page a title, a description and a favicon
→ Delete all placeholder text

For effort, follow Anthropic's cost guide from yesterday: medium is for well-scoped daily work. The default medium is enough for these 20 fixes; raise it for the harder ones. Thariq tested it: turning effort up mostly buys more verification and edge-case testing.

Send this whole post to Claude Code. If you need to, add this line at the end 👇
"Send one subagent per group to check it without editing anything. Then fix everything yourself from their lists, so no two agents edit the same file. If a group is more complex, raise that subagent's effort. Show me the list of issues first, don't change anything until I confirm, and when you're done, give me before-and-after screenshots."

quotedTweet.text:
Anthropic just published its 𝗳𝘂𝗹𝗹 𝗰𝗼𝘀𝘁 𝗴𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗲 for Opus 5.5. You can ask Opus 5.5 to use it to review your Claude Code setup.

At the same effort level, Opus 5.5 thinks more per turn than Opus 5, most of all at xhigh and max. Thinking is billed as output, and an output token costs 𝟭𝟬𝟬 𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲𝘀 𝗮 𝗰𝗮𝗰𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱. So don't carry over the level you set for Opus 5. Start at medium, and save xhigh and max for work where you've measured a gain.

Send this prompt to Opus 5.5 👇

"Read this guide: https://t.co/8RHkfmiKjM

Then review my Claude Code setup against it: my user and project settings, the subagents in ~/.claude/agents and .claude/agents, CLAUDE.md, and the MCP servers I have connected. Find three kinds of problems:
1. A default effort that doesn't fit the work. Use the guide's ladder: low for mechanical edits, medium for well-scoped daily work, high when medium stalls, and xhigh or max only for work where a gain was measured. Flag a default of xhigh or max, or a level I picked for Opus 5. Then look at this project's code and recent commits and tell me which kinds of work here fit which level.
2. Subagents that only search, read logs or run tests but set no model, so they run on my main model.
3. Setup that makes every turn cost more: MCP servers I don't use, or a CLAUDE.md well over 200 lines.

For each issue, quote the setting or line, explain what it costs, and suggest the smallest change. Also tell me which three things to check in /usage at the end of a task.

Show me the recommendations first. Don't change anything yet."

text:
Ten million people have watched a Stanford lecturer accidentally destroy the entire self-help industry.

He filmed the lecture once as his Last Lecture to Stanford's Class of 2026.

Life coaches charge $500 an hour to teach a diluted version of what he covered in 33 minutes for free.

His name is Graham Weaver. He is a lecturer at the Stanford Graduate School of Business and the founder of Alpine Investors, a private equity firm managing $16 billion of institutional capital.

Every year at Stanford GSB, he gives graduating students a lecture called "How to Win Without Crushing Your Soul."

His entire framework fits on a napkin.

Achievement does not fix self-hatred. External wins taste like salt water. Fire the inner coach who uses fear as motivation. What you avoid grows. Pull the nails out of your head. Trust the second voice, the one that speaks through energy, not panic.

That last rule alone has probably cost the hustle culture industry a hundred million dollars.

"The good old days are happening right now, unless you skip them."

That is the closing line of the lecture. Weaver spent thirty years running past his to figure it out.

Founders raise $100 million and cry in their car the day the round closes because the number was supposed to fix them and did not. Engineers earn their first six-figure promotion and lose sleep the same night because the person the raise was supposed to save is still there.

The lecture is free on Stanford GSB's YouTube channel. Weaver's writing is free on his newsletter.

Weaver still lectures at Stanford. Almost none of the ten million viewers have actually fired their inner coach.

The framework is free. The willingness to actually trust the second voice before your next promotion, exit, or investor meeting is the entire edge.

text:
面试被问了几次这种系统设计题目：
企业级 AI Agent 调用与计费平台，峰值 2 万 QPS，任务最长跑几十分钟，要解决长任务、高并发额度扣减、计费准确性和高可用。

🤔2万 QPS 是入口峰值，但单个 Agent 任务要跑几十分钟。这意味着同时在跑的任务量 = 2 万 × 30 分钟 ≈ 几十万。HTTP 连接绝对不能挂在那等结果。

链路核心是 "快进快出"：Gateway 鉴权限流 → Redis 预扣额度 → 丢进 MQ → 立刻返回 task_id。 Agent 在后台慢慢跑，前端轮询或 WebSocket 拿结果。同步请求只做 "接单"，不做 "执行"。

额度扣减，Agent 任务要跑几十分钟，你在入口根本不知道最终消耗多少 token、调了几次工具，凭什么先扣？

两个扣款阶段： 
① 入口冻结一个上限额度（按模型档位 × 预估 token 上限），写一条冻结单 
② 任务跑完，按实际用量真扣，多冻结的释放回去；任务失败就直接释放 冻结是为了防超额，结算才是真扣，两件事分开。

用量是多维的：token、工具调用次数、执行时长、模型档位，分别埋点上报
冻结和结算用同一个口径，不会出现 "冻结按 A 算、结算按 B 算" 的对不上
失败任务分场景：LLM 调用失败全额释放冻结，部分工具调用失败按已完成部分结算
全链路幂等，任务重试不会重复冻结或重复扣

高可用的关键不在 Gateway，在任务状态：
调度器挂了，跑了一半的几十万任务怎么办？
任务状态必须持久化，重启后能从断点恢复。
MQ 削峰，失败任务单独隔离，自动释放额度并通知用户。

text:
为什么现在顶尖的 AI Agent 团队都在聚焦 Harness Engineering（运行时支架工程）？

很多人以为构建 Agent 只是选一个高智力基座模型，配上一组 Prompt 和几个 API 接口。但在真实复杂的长链路场景（如自动化代码重构、多步数据分析）中，模型能力只是系统及格线，Harness 才是决定产品成败的关键。

当模型开始读取文件、调用工具、修改外部环境并多步递进时，围绕在模型外层的软件架构面临着极高的系统工程要求：

上下文生命周期管理：任务越长，历史记录越臃肿。全量保留不仅成本飙升，还会稀释注意力。Harness 必须做出裁决：哪些留存在 Context 中，哪些总结压缩，哪些沉淀为外部持久状态按需检索。

确定性执行与安全沙箱：模型给出的只是“调用意图”。Harness 必须负责资源鉴权、副作用隔离、执行监控与操作拦截，避免代理在误判下产生破坏性后果。

断点恢复与容错状态机：长运行任务必然遭遇网络波动、工具报错或人为中断。系统必须具备状态快照与检查点机制，支持断点重试与轨迹回放，而不是一出错就推倒重来。

可观测性与精准调试：当 Agent 失败时，换模型通常无法根治问题。真正起效的改进往往在于重构工具接口粒度、优化信息注入格式，或在运行时增加失败兜底逻辑。

随着模型能力逐渐成为标配，单纯靠 Prompt 调优的红利正在迅速见顶。如何构建可观察、可测试、具备确定性容错能力的 Harness，把不可控的概率推断封装为工业级可靠的执行流水线，才是下一阶段 AI 架构师的核心护城河。

This is really smart.

There are definitely a set of rules that are too complex to lint deterministically that feel wasted on full-scale intelligence.

- Using useEffect in sensible ways
- Keeping good comments while killing bad ones

quotedTweet.text:
I’ve been experimenting a bit with Jev as a fuzzy linter that runs after edits in your agent harness: looks very promising so far in my evals.

First I converted all of our coding guidelines to tiny rules that are very easy to judge.

Then, only kept the ones that don’t require extra context/files/reasoning. I want it to be a single call, super fast, and Jev isn’t smart enough to handle complex or ambiguous rules.

I then created a synthetic eval that has different kinds of tool calls to exercise and test every one of those rules. Also a held out set that we don’t train on so we don’t accidentally overfit (ie benchmax).

One cool thing that seems to work well: Jev returns confidence, so in addition to high confidence violations, we can also return medium confidence and get the agent to double check.

Adding that lower confidence tier seems to double what it catches, and only increases false positives a little.

I still have yet to test this inside an actual agent to see how the agent reacts to this feedback. Hopefully next week I can get a decent eval going and see how well this works E2E.

📓 真香！Obsidian 多设备同步这件事，Self-hosted LiveSync 让你自己当服务器，官方同步的月费可以省下来了。

GitHub 1.2 万 star，MIT 开源，光是这个月就连发了五个版本。

场景很具体：手机上随手记了几条，回到电脑想接着写。以前两条路，要么交官方同步的订阅费，要么塞进网盘让它自己同步——后者的下场通常是一堆冲突文件，同一篇笔记躺着三个版本，你还得手动挑。Self-hosted LiveSync 的做法是自己挂一个后端，CouchDB 可以，MinIO、S3、Cloudflare R2 这类对象存储也行，简单冲突它自己合并，传输走端到端加密。

更省事的是它连设置、代码片段、主题和插件都能一起同步，换台机器不用重新配一遍。它也支持用 WebRTC 点对点同步，设备之间直接交换笔记，只是还需要一个中继帮它们互相发现。

有两件事得说清楚：它和官方的 Obsidian Sync 不互通，装了就是走自己这条路；1.0 版本要求 Obsidian 1.7.2 以上。

笔记这种东西，存在自己手里才睡得着。

GitHub：https://t.co/zpkwS2tzza

text:
高中曾经发生一件炸裂的事情。

午休的间隙，一名男同学偷偷钻进广播室，接通了全校的广播。

他的声音顺着喇叭传遍整栋教学楼：“原本今天安排的播音取消了，我想占用大家几分钟，宣布一件事。”

我坐在教室里，心一下子悬了起来。

会是什么事？是受了委屈要控诉学校？还是和谁闹了矛盾，要当众对峙？我盯着教室的喇叭，等着一场风波。

紧接着，他开始念一个个名字。

我心里咯噔一下，立刻猜想：难道是要当众表白？

“高一三班的同学，谢谢你当初借我钱吃饭。”

“门卫大叔，谢谢你午休晚归那次，装作没看见我，没有登记上报。”

“数学老师，谢谢你那次单独留我谈话，没有打电话通知我家长。”

“食堂卖面的大叔，谢谢你很长一段时间，每次都多给我一勺肉。”

教室里零星响起几声哄笑，我慢慢安静下来。就在我以为这是一场公开的道谢时，他又开口了。

“明天，我就不来上学了。”

广播里继续传来他的声音：“老师们总说读书的机会难得，我没法继续在这里念书了。以前我不懂，现在挺羡慕还坐在教室里的你们。”

原来是家里出了变故，他已经办好退学手续，准备外出打工。

短暂停顿之后。

“下午还要上课，大家好好听课。”

广播直接中断。

不到十分钟，年级主任、保安还有几位老师急匆匆冲进广播室，男生早就离开了。

听说校长原本打算严肃处分他，得知他已经退学，最后没有再追究。

这件事最让我记到现在的，是第二天。

广播站照常中午播音，播报完天气和校园通知。播音员收尾时，突然多了一句话：

“昨天广播里的那位同学，如果你还在校，请到教务处一趟。”

现在搭建个人 VPN 节点，真的只要 5 分钟了

1. 购买一个 VPS 服务器，CN2 GIA最好。拿到 ssh 的账号密码

2. 发给 Agent这段 Prompt：
“ssh  root@xx.xx.xx.xx，密码是XXXXX，根据https://t.co/hhzxnktyUE 给这台VPS 服务器安装 Vless + reality，然后把可导入 V2rayN 的 分享地址发给我”
为了安全，安装后建议换 ssh 密码

3. 在电脑上安装 V2rayN
https://t.co/i5CgBn4VIa

4. 在 V2rayN 界面把第二步的链接粘贴进去，结束了，开始用你的独享节点

感慨，还记得2020 年跟着不良林老师，用 vultr + x-ui +vmess 一步步搭建，搞了半天才搞定😭

text:
做医疗 AI 的朋友，可以看看这个开源数据集。

HuggingFace 上用 Claude Opus 5.5 生成的 2194 种疾病的模拟医患对话，平均每段 33 轮，从描述症状、检查，一直聊到治疗和后续安排。

这里有个有意思的设计：每段对话里，患者都会故意隐瞒一件事，或者说一句假话，医生得通过追问发现问题，再把信息纠正过来。这个细节很关键。现实里患者可能不会把所有信息整理得清清楚楚再来问你。作者还给数据加了校验。

可以直接拿来做医疗对话训练、微调小模型，或者研究医疗知识检索。不过它依然是合成数据，引用查得到，也不代表医学结论就一定正确。

https://t.co/EjH1MEoeew

text:
有没有连接所有科学的桥梁？

@nntaleb 老师的回答只有一个词：概率论。

硅谷传奇投资人 @naval  那句“1000 个平行宇宙里，要做到在 999 个里富有”，讲的也是这个。

这里也推荐五本书，从易到难：

1.《醉汉的脚步》这本书故事多，公式少，趣味性很足
2.《随机漫步的傻瓜》俄罗斯轮盘实验就是他的思路，只看结果论英雄，迟早会陷入运气的诅咒
3.《对赌》职业扑克手教你把每个决定当成一次下注
4.《与天为敌》人类怎么一步步驯服风险，从赌桌一路讲到保险和华尔街
5.《Introduction to Probability》哈佛 Stat 110 的教材，不过教材嘛，你懂的

5 分钟动画附在下面 👇

quotedTweet.text:
有人问 @nntaleb 老师，世上可有一门秘密科学连接其他所有学科，塔勒布老师答：概率论。顺着这条思路，让Gemini推荐了两本入门书。

- Feller 的《An Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications》第一卷 。它不需要您具备高深的微积分或测度论知识，却能用极其精妙的例子（如硬币抛掷的随机游走、破产问题等）向您展示概率法则在现实世界中是如何运作的。

- 配合阅读 Ian Hacking 的《The Emergence of Probability》，您会对科学的本质产生全新的认知。

text:
Claude Code tip: before you ship, have Opus 5.5 send out 𝟰 𝘀𝘂𝗯𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 whose only job is to break your app, and split 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘀𝗲 𝟭𝟲 𝗾𝘂𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 between them:

Security
→ Do your bundled frontend JS or git history contain private keys like sk_ or service_role?
→ Skip the UI and call your APIs directly, logged out or with someone else's ID. Does the server stop you?
→ Change the price, quantity or role in a request and send it again. Does the server accept it?
→ Hit the same endpoint 100 times in a row. Is there a rate limit per user and IP?
→ Hide a snippet that pops an alert in Markdown, rich text or an uploaded SVG. Does it run when another account opens it?

Data
→ Load 10,000 records. Does the page still open?
→ Use a 200-character name with emoji. Does it break the layout?
→ Sign up with the same email in different capitalization. Did you just get two accounts?
→ Submit an empty form. Is there now a blank record in your database?

Flows
→ Place the same order twice at once, and replay the same payment webhook twice. Did you get two orders?
→ Refresh or hit Back halfway through a form. Is what you typed still there?
→ Save while offline: it says saved, but nothing was stored
→ Upload a 50MB image. Does everything freeze?

Environment
→ On a small phone screen at 200% zoom, can you still tap every button?
→ Switch to Safari's engine. Does the layout fall apart?
→ For users in other time zones, are dates, deadlines and check-ins off by a day?

Set all 4 subagents to high effort. The security one covers payments and login, where one mistake is a disaster, so you can raise it to xhigh or even max. Anthropic's Thariq has said that turning effort up mostly buys more verification and edge-case testing.

Send this whole post to Claude Code, and add this line at the end 👇
"Create 4 testing subagents in ~/.claude/agents, one for each group above: security-breaker, data-breaker, flow-breaker and env-breaker. Use model opus for all of them, effort high, and xhigh for security-breaker. Give them permission only to read files, run commands and use a browser (Playwright), with no changes to code or config. Install Playwright first if it's missing.
Before every launch, run the app locally or in a test environment and have each of them work through its group item by item. If login is needed, ask me for two test accounts first. Use payment test mode only. Mock the AI APIs, or use a test key with a spending cap. Write test data only to a test database and clean it up afterwards. If you find production keys or a live domain, stop immediately and ask me.
For every issue, write the steps to reproduce, a screenshot and the fix. Combine them, rank them by severity and hand them to the main session to fix. Mark anything you can't test as "untested" with the reason. Show me the files you'll create first, and don't write them until I confirm."

quotedTweet.text:
Claude Code tip: before you ship a vibe-coded site, have Opus 5.5 send out 𝟱 𝘀𝘂𝗯𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 to check 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘀𝗲 𝟮𝟬 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴𝘀, then fix them all in one pass:

Consistent design
→ Write a DESIGN.md first, and make every color, font size, spacing and corner radius follow it
→ Keep the palette restrained and the type hierarchy clear
→ Make every button, card and input of the same kind look alike
→ Too flat? Add emphasis. Too crowded? Cut
→ Keep text readable on both dark and light backgrounds

On mobile
→ No sideways scrolling, and nothing spilling off the screen
→ Add a mobile menu
→ Make buttons big enough to tap
→ Keep the layout intact when the text is enlarged

Every state
→ Give loading, empty and error states a proper screen
→ Give every button feedback, with its own hover, pressed and disabled look
→ Show form errors right where they happen, plus submitting, success and failure messages
→ Add transitions to modals, dropdowns and tab switches

Use it like a real user
→ Click through the core flows, like sign-up and checkout, from start to finish
→ Find buttons that do nothing and links that are broken
→ Make sure the whole thing works with just a keyboard

Before launch
→ Say what you do in one line on the home page
→ Give each page one main button you want people to click
→ Give every page a title, a description and a favicon
→ Delete all placeholder text

For effort, follow Anthropic's cost guide from yesterday: medium is for well-scoped daily work. The default medium is enough for these 20 fixes; raise it for the harder ones. Thariq tested it: turning effort up mostly buys more verification and edge-case testing.

Send this whole post to Claude Code. If you need to, add this line at the end 👇
"Send one subagent per group to check it without editing anything. Then fix everything yourself from their lists, so no two agents edit the same file. If a group is more complex, raise that subagent's effort. Show me the list of issues first, don't change anything until I confirm, and when you're done, give me before-and-after screenshots."

这个开源缠论工具有点开挂：分型、笔、中枢不用手画，程序直接标出来。

学缠论最劝退的不是理论，是自己画笔和中枢。每个人画得不一样，回测还没开始，标注先吵起来。

分享一个开源项目：czsc，支持 A股、期货和加密。

它把缠中说禅那套分型、笔、中枢做成可计算的工具。K 线丢进去，结构自动标，还能生成信号、做多级别联立和回测。

✅ 自动识别分型、笔、中枢，不用一张张手动画

✅ 200+ 信号函数，事件可以按条件组合

✅ 多级别联立，1 分钟合成 5 分钟、30 分钟、日线一起看

✅ 权重回测，能算手续费，导出 HTML 报告

✅ 核心算法迁到 Rust，Python 直接调用

仓库地址：https://t.co/jjOX28H8Zr

仅做开源工具分享，非投资建议。DYOR

这个开源 A 股复盘神器太省事了！

涨停池、连板梯队、龙虎榜、板块资金，一套全包，还能帮你整理盘面逻辑！

每天收盘后，翻涨停、查龙虎榜、看板块、整理复盘，资料散在几个页面里，来回切就很费时间。

这个开源项目：Vibe AStock。

把 A 股盯盘、盘后复盘、个股研究和交易记录，放进同一个本地网页。

✅ 涨停池 + 连板梯队：昨天的强势股今天谁晋级、谁断板、谁回落，集中跟踪。

✅ 盘中异动追踪：根据行情快照整理急拉急跌、封板开板等变化，查看自选股和板块动态。

✅ AI 盘后复盘：围绕市场情绪、资金、题材、龙虎榜和龙头跟踪，整理分析依据与后续观察条件。

✅ 个股研究 + 多空辩论：结合行情、估值、财报和研报资料，对照不同观点，不只听一个结论。

✅ 自选股 + 交易日志：关注什么、为什么买、后面表现怎么样，和研究记录放在一起。

它不是让 AI 对着股票代码自由发挥。行情和统计由程序处理，AI 再根据资料做解读，复盘时还能查看依据。

text:
想要重塑金钱认知，一部纪录片就能带来巨大改变。

推荐Netflix高分作品《聪明生活经济学》，看完很多人对财富的理解都会被颠覆。

孔乙提取片中核心理财思路，帮大家建立通往财务自由的底层观念。

1. 精简开支
定期复盘账单，找出外卖、冲动消费、高价课程这类无效支出，砍掉不必要的花销。

2. 做好资产规划
收入多少不等于财富多少，无论薪资高低，都要对资金做分类管理。

3. 拒绝即时享乐
不要被短期快感绑架，远离借贷超前消费。单独开立储蓄账户，坚持理性消费。

4. 树立家庭财富认知
一家人的消费与理财习惯，会潜移默化塑造下一代的金钱观。

5. 理性按需消费
下单前预估使用频率，就算价格低廉，低频闲置的物品也不要入手。

片子里有一句很扎心的结论，单纯死存钱，财富只会不断被通胀侵蚀。

不妨静下心问问自己，五年之后，你期待什么样的生活。

下面整理11部提升富人思维的纪录片，普通人可以慢慢学习搞钱逻辑。

1.《隐形亿万富翁》
富豪拿着100美元和旧车从零起步，三个月搭建百万规模企业，读懂目标感与执行力的价值。

2.《金钱与我》
理财专家一对一解决普通人财务难题，存钱、买房、养老的实操省钱办法都有覆盖。

3.《富哥哥穷弟弟》
对比两兄弟截然不同的人生，看懂认知差异，是同龄人拉开阶层差距的关键。

4.《金钱通解》
拆解市面上各类金融陷阱与消费套路，学会守住自身本金。

5.《成为沃伦巴菲特》
褪去投资神话滤镜，理解股神的自律、财富理念与长期主义。

6.《无节制消费的元凶》
撕开商家营销底层套路，克制冲动消费，养成储蓄习惯。

7.《超级顾客》
扒开各类消费智商税，识别营销噱头，掌握实用的消费省钱技巧。

8.《十分钟速成课：经济学》
通俗讲解经济学基础知识，零基础人群可以快速入门。

9.《致富之道》
走访世界各地顶尖富豪，看懂不同圈层的赚钱模式。

10.《美国商业大亨传奇》
讲述五位商业巨头的崛起故事，拓宽个人商业视野。

11.《为什么贫穷》
直面社会现实差距，看懂贫穷背后隐藏的底层逻辑。

后续会持续筛选优质财经纪录片，持续升级大家的财商认知。

希望本次分享对你有帮助，我是孔乙，复旦经济学博士，关注我，每天低频高质拆解宏观经济与投资技巧。

text:
🔥别再让 Opus 5.5 全程满血烧钱了！Jev 当裁判、Opus 干硬活，成本和时间直接砍掉约 80%！现在还不搭建，才是真看不懂！

核心亮点
🔹Opus 只负责难推理；Jev 从 harness 预先准备好的选项里做选择并校验
🔹动态调 effort（low→max），用 per-message 声明改力度，不打碎 prompt cache
🔹失败自动升档、通过自动降档，工具挂了先选恢复路径，不全量重跑
🔹先筛项目笔记再灌上下文，简单任务分流给更快 worker
🔹先跑聚焦检查，再上完整测试套件

两条上手路径（选一条就行）
A. 最快：给 Claude Code 加上 Jev 决策层
仓库：https://t.co/C1EIlS81aY
1️⃣准备 Node ≥ 22.18 + Claude Code 2.1.280+（先 claude auth login）
2️⃣npm install -g jev-opus
3️⃣jev-opus init（填 TypeSafe / OpenRouter 的 Jev key；没有也能用本地启发式）
4️⃣jev-opus doctor 体检
5️⃣jev-opus claude 启动，在 /model 选 Opus 5.5 · Jev
6️⃣开始干活。想无头跑任务：jev-opus "fix the failing tests"

B. 完整 harness：本地工作区 + 决策层
仓库：https://t.co/L3nF1WftUN
工程说明：https://t.co/xakbOgyuZO
1️⃣Apple Silicon + macOS 15+
2️⃣git clone https://t.co/8OHHTc87iR && cd keel
3️⃣bash scripts/build-laya-assets.sh
4️⃣cargo build -p keel --bin keel --release
5️⃣打开 Keel，选 Jev / Local Laya / Normal
6️⃣接上你已有的 Claude Code / Codex / Cursor 等 agent，把决策交给 Jev，推理交给 Opus

原则就一句： harness 准备选项并校验，Jev 做窄决策，Opus 5.5 只在值得烧的地方满血。

💥炸了！斯坦福×英伟达开源 CLM 把 Jev 按在地上摩擦：决策最快快 13 倍，还不写字，只比向量！

Agent 每一步都要从候选动作里挑一个，大模型逐 token 写答案太慢。CLM 换思路：把当前局面和每个候选动作分别编码成向量，谁更近选谁；动作向量还能提前算好缓存，候选越多，优势越大。

跟点对比 3 个实例：
🔹恐龙跑酷：CLM 一次决策 16ms vs Jev 150ms，快约 9 倍，零样本照样过关

🔹Super Mario：CLM 约 4 倍更快（33.5ms vs 132.6ms），两边都能通关

🔹WikiRacing：从「板块构造」点到「生物发光」，CLM 79.8ms vs Jev 225ms；微调当「裁判」后，DeepSWE 挑中方案通过率 81.6%（Jev 71.1%），还快 5.7 倍

代价也很清楚：它只能在给定候选里挑，不会自己发明新动作。

开源、单卡能跑，System One 这条路被彻底打开了。

text:
AI 正在彻底重塑学术研究的底层逻辑。Google 推出的全新多智能体科研框架 ScientistTwo，实现了完全无需人类参与（Zero Human-in-the-loop）的端到端自主科研。

传统科研往往需要学者耗费数月甚至数年推进，而面对 ScientistTwo，研究者只需给出一个核心科学命题，它就能全自动跑通科研全链路：

文献调研与立项：自主检索海量前沿学术文献，快速确立 Baseline 并提炼出全新的科学假说；

实验设计与落地：自主编写高质量代码，调度计算资源运行实验，并执行严谨的消融实验（Ablation Studies）；

论文撰写与自我评审：自动生成专家级学术论文，并与模拟同行评审引擎开展多轮对抗与学术辩论，主动修补漏洞直至达到顶会标准。

更令人震惊的是它的实测表现。在直面 NeurIPS、ICML 等顶级学术会议的人类巅峰成果时，ScientistTwo 在 86 项基准任务中全面超越人类顶尖水平（SOTA），平均性能提升幅度高达 25.2%！整个过程没有出现任何虚构引用的“幻觉”，所有代码均通过全量验证且可直接执行。

过去两年，行业普遍把大模型当做编写辅助代码、提炼文献摘要的“高级实习生”。但 ScientistTwo 的出现宣告了这个阶段的终结——它不再只是科研副驾驶，而是一个正在主动拓展人类认知边界的“自主科学拓荒者”。

当 AI 已经能够自主提出假说、验证实验并产出突破性论文时，距离它发现连人类现有科学体系与数学语言都尚未定义的全新规律，究竟还有多久？

text:
I checked my laptop before bed and almost dropped it. $239 had turned into $4,373 while I did literally nothing all day.

didn't touch it once. Grok Bot blew past its own $1,500 target before lunch and just kept going for another 14 hours because nobody told it to stop.

what actually got me is it's making money two different ways at once now:

> trading memecoins the same way it always has
> launched its own token on the side and collects fees off the volume trading through it

so it's earning even on the hours where a trade doesn't work out. one stream doesn't need the other to be right.

five clean exits carried almost half the day's profit on their own. the rest was just the quiet grind underneath, small fills and fee income stacking up while I wasn't even looking, nothing dramatic on any single one of them but it never stopped moving the whole session.

win rate sitting comfortably above 80%, and it didn't need one big lucky call to get there, it needed five good ones and a lot of patience in between.

I sat there refreshing the app twice like it was going to correct itself. it didn't. $239 turned into $4,373 and I have no f*cking clue how I'm supposed to go back to watching a chart by hand after seeing this.

text:
Ten million people have watched an MIT professor accidentally destroy the executive coaching industry.

He filmed the lecture once in January 2018 and died eighteen months later.

Executive coaches charge fifteen thousand dollars a session to teach a third of what he covered in one hour for free.

His name was Patrick Winston. He ran the MIT Artificial Intelligence Laboratory from 1972 to 1997 and wrote the AI textbook every computer science major in the world read for thirty years.

Every January for four decades, he gave a lecture called "How to Speak."

His entire framework fits on a napkin.

Do not read. Be in the image. Keep images simple. Eliminate clutter. Start with an empathetic connection. End with a punch line the audience can repeat over dinner. Never open with a joke. Never end with "thank you."

That last rule alone has probably cost the executive coaching industry a hundred million dollars.

"Your success in life will be determined largely by your ability to speak, your ability to write, and the quality of your ideas. In that order."

That is the actual opening line of the lecture. Winston believed it strongly enough to spend fifty years teaching computer scientists how to talk.

Founders spend $80,000 on an MBA and then hire a communications coach to teach them the same material Winston filmed once for free. Engineers write brilliant code and lose promotions to teammates who watched this lecture on the train.

The lecture is free on MIT OpenCourseWare. The textbook is free on his page.

Winston died in 2019. Almost none of the ten million viewers have actually implemented the four rules on the napkin.

The napkin is free. The willingness to actually use it in your next meeting is the entire edge.

text:
🗒️ 又发现一个后台神器 shadcn-admin，接活要做管理后台的话，界面这部分基本可以省了。

GitHub 揽获 1.4 万 star，两千两百多个 fork，MIT 许可证，拿去随便改。

想一下这个场景：接了个小项目要做后台，第一天几乎全花在搭壳子上——左边侧边栏、明暗主题切换、路由、几张表格页、一个全局搜索框，一样一样搭，两三天过去，正事一行没写。shadcn-admin 把这一整套做完了，十几个页面现成，侧边栏是内置组件，明暗主题和响应式都在里面，连从右到左语言的排版和无障碍适配都做了。

作者 satnaing 特意声明这不是脚手架模板，意思是别指望一条命令生成项目，它是一套做完的成品界面，你对着拆、按需改。底层是 Shadcn UI 那一套加 Vite、TanStack Router 和 TypeScript，登录部分接的是 Clerk。

前端最不值钱的时间就是重复搭壳子，这种活能省一天算一天。

GitHub：https://t.co/E56j5A4e7N

text:
🔥 黄仁勋最新访谈：我的底层思维，来自3本书

最近，黄仁勋做客《纽约时报》播客，在英伟达圣塔克拉拉总部展开了一场深度对话。当业界大佬纷纷拉响“AI末日警报”时，身处产业链核心的老黄却展现出截然不同的工程师现实主义。

以下是笔记侠整理的精华内容，帮你快速Get这位AI教父的核心判断👇

一、AI这场工业革命，钱到底在哪？

老黄把AI产业比作五层蛋糕：

能源 → 芯片/AI工厂 → 基础设施/云服务 → 模型层 → 应用层（最值钱！）

医疗、法律、制造、金融……所有传统行业从这一层接入技术红利。用户摸到的是软件，底下压着的是电和芯片。

💡 职业不会消失，消失的是重复任务

- 放射科医生没消失，消失的是“读片”——算法接手筛查，医生腾出精力处理复杂病例，医院吞吐量反而上升。
- 程序员没消失，消失的是“手写代码”——工程师的灵魂在于工程，而非敲代码。工具剥离日常任务，让人更专注系统架构与价值创造。

二、就业与开源：两笔被算错的账

❌ 工作量不是固定大小的饼

很多人静态推导：自动化进去→工时减少→大批失业。却忽略了经济运行的核心变量：人类的野心。

效率释放后，人的野心会开辟更大的新需求。过去50年，康养、高端文娱、个性化旅游等新行业不断涌现。

✅ 技术门槛正在抹平

过去用计算机得啃C++、CUDA；现在自然语言就是接口。全球一两千万程序员拥有的数字化生产力，正平等下放给数十亿人。最划算的做法：尽快把AI放进工作流，做那个会用杠杆的人。

🔓 开源不是慈善，是产业底座

英伟达以超120亿美元估值收购HuggingFace，逻辑很清晰：AI模型将成为每个国家、每家企业的核心底座。开源能确保网络安全，也让全球开发者共建生态。中国工程师基数庞大，在开源落地上正形成强大飞轮。

三、末日论？既不明智，也不负责任

辛顿预言“AI终结文明概率10%”，老黄直言：这个数字没有任何严谨科学支撑，只是个人直觉。

- 几年前辛顿还说“5年内放射科医生全失业”，结果呢？
- 靠制造恐慌吸引眼球，让年轻人对高等教育失去信心，绝不是社会责任。
- Scaling Law（规模法则）边际效应已放缓，全行业正转向推理期规模法则（Test-time Scaling）。
- 软件哪来的自主意志？ 它消耗的只是电网送来的电，电源一断就是硅片。大模型本质是超大规模矩阵运算，完全可以用工程手段拆解、修正。

四、钱、管制和电力，三笔大账

⚠️ 算力泡沫？ 两三年内不会逆转。英伟达正把资源下沉到应用层，让实体经济从AI中榨出真金白银，才能形成稳固商业闭环。

🌍 中美AI竞争： 美国强在模型前沿，中国胜在应用普及。衡量工业革命成功的标准，不是实验室跑分，而是全社会产业扩散深度。

🔋 能源真相： 未来3-5年不得不靠天然气填缺口；但放到10年周期，AI正成为全球清洁能源革命最强商业推手——数百亿风投正涌入先进核能、地热、长时储能。就像外科手术，恢复前总要先挨那一刀。

五、我的底层思维，来自3本书 📚

老黄面对AI狂热的全部工具箱：

1. 《计算机体系结构：定量研究方法》 ——把抽象系统拆成可验证的工程问题
2. 《创新者的窘境》 ——看懂颠覆性技术的真实节奏，建立理性商业预期
3. 《定位》 ——理解人心智如何认知信息，在纷繁中精准锚定战略卡位

老黄最后说：

Agent没有让你少思考，它只是逼着你把思考前置，然后替你做执行。
看地图代替不了行军，学AI最重要的是在自己的真实业务里跑通一遍。把第一个自动化设起来，把第一个十倍效率场景落在自己公司身上。

text:
it's f*cking gold

TypeSafe just dropped the official skill that teaches Claude Code to build on Jev

left alone, coding agents ask Jev one question per call and guess the field names.

this skill rewires the order before a single line gets written:

docs -> behaviour -> judgments -> one request -> code decides

every rule in it, broken down on two pages:

> see the failure behind each of its 11 instructions
> pick Choice, Noul or Score in one glance
> paste the prompt skeleton straight into your agent

12.2x

the bill drop when 13 questions share one call, measured in TypeSafe's cookbook.

a short file that does a lot of the thinking for your agent.

quotedTweet.text:
it's f*cking insane

Jev sat between GPT and me, killing every draft that broke my rules before i saw it. good setup.

then Jev did not answer. the agent decided silence was safer and stopped sending me anything at all. took a second agent to unstick it.

your checker needs a branch for the moment it goes quiet:

> let it through tagged unverified and keep moving
> hand the risky span to the big model
> park it in a queue and retry in a minute
> wake a human when the action is irreversible

70-500 ms

one Jev call, by TypeSafe's own number. a half-second checker still takes down the whole pipeline when it has no default.

text:
Everyone's posting motion videos made with Opus 5.5, and they're wild. To make one yourself in Claude Code, give it 𝗮 𝟰-𝗽𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗲𝗮𝗺, with each subagent owning one part end to end:

→ Breakdown (medium): tile frames from a reference video you love into one image, pull out its pacing, type and transitions, and write them up as HyperFrames code. Find references on https://t.co/6WlRF4Ln7m, which has 2,000+ product launch videos
→ Storyboard (medium): lay out 3 storyboard options in one image for you to pick from, then make one still per scene for the one you choose
→ Build (main session, high): write every scene as HyperFrames code, add music, and render a draft before the final
→ Review (high): watch the render second by second and list the problems by severity, without touching anything

You just 𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗹 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗵𝗼𝘁𝘀 𝗹𝗶𝗸𝗲 𝗮 𝗱𝗶𝗿𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗼𝗿: "slow this part down by half", "cut right here", "zoom in on the button".

The black hole lab quoted below was made by Opus 5.5 too: one prompt for the first version, then I went to sleep while a few agents took turns finding and fixing problems, and woke up to three rounds done. My short animation "small print" also came from Opus 5.5. My first prompt asked it to break down a reference video, and after rendering, it went back over the result second by second and polished it.

Send this prompt to Claude Code 👇

"Set up a motion video team in ~/.claude/agents that I can use for every product video. If HyperFrames isn't installed, install it first following https://t.co/FymJe8Xlht.

1. reference-breaker (effort: medium): use ffmpeg to pull one frame per second from the reference video I give you, tile them into one image to look at, and break down the pacing, type, colors and transitions into a shot list plus HyperFrames starter code. Break down only; don't build.
2. storyboarder (effort: medium): from the shot list, make 3 storyboard options with a few key frames each, tiled into one image for me to pick from. After I pick one, use npx hyperframes snapshot to make one still per scene.
3. The main session builds the video: write each scene in HyperFrames, and if there's no music, synthesize a track with Python. Render a draft with npx hyperframes render --quality draft first, and render the final only after I approve.
4. film-reviewer (effort: high): use ffmpeg to pull one frame per second and review it second by second. List problems as P0, P1 and P2 (P0 must be fixed). Review only; don't edit. The main session fixes every P0 before showing me.

Every subagent needs Bash and must be able to view images. Before starting, ask me for the reference video, logo, colors, fonts and product screenshots. Show me the contents of the files you'll create, then explain the flow in words a 10-year-old could follow. Don't write anything until I confirm."

quotedTweet.text:
I asked Opus 5.5 to explain gravitational lensing by building an interactive black hole lab

One prompt for the first version, then a dynamic workflow to polish it for three rounds while I slept. This is what I woke up to: 5h 28m end to end, $90 at API prices

https://t.co/BE1xui93rF

Drag the black hole and the sky behind it bends into arcs, closing into a full ring when everything lines up

Each round ran 3 agents. Two reviewers each picked 9 to 10 issues and ranked them P0, P1, P2. The third one fixed them.
Round 1: 3D materials and lighting + UI and type
Round 2: camera motion and interaction + science-communication design
Round 3: a design director deciding whether it ships + visual QA and performance

Every P0 got fixed, the rest only if worth it. When the two reviewers disagreed, it picked one and wrote down why. It backed up before each round, checked screenshots after, and rolled back anything it couldn't fix.

text:
Hiring Tony Robbins today costs 1 million dollars for just one day.

This is a 21-minute tape recorded in his own home more than 30 years ago.
There, he explains exactly how to get anyone to say yes.
The same material for which they now charge a fortune... completely free.

It's a rare, unfiltered recording from the time when he still didn't charge millionaires just for being in the same room.

When someone says no, they give two excuses:
“I don’t have time” or “I don’t have money”
Neither is true.

The real reason is that they still don’t believe it’s worth it.
It’s not a money problem. It’s a state problem.

Tony teaches something he calls “attack and confess”
Instead of arguing the objection, you confess your own:

“I had the chance to go six months ago and I didn’t until two months ago.
I can’t even imagine the time I wasted”

The room goes silent. No one argues.

Then he gets the person on the “yes train”
Each little yes adds to the next.
Until saying no at the end feels harder than saying yes.

When it’s time to sign, the person has already said yes five times without realizing it.

Just 21 minutes.
There you learn the two only moves that people pay 1 million a day for:
how to read anyone’s state… and how to shift it.

Most people spend years guessing in sales.
He wrote it on a flipchart in his living room in less than half an hour.

A seat in that room cost $125 dollars.
Today it costs $1 million dollars a day to sit in front of him.

The tape is free right now.
And the answer is in this video.

text:
兄弟们，昨晚通宵测了一下浙大刚开源的这个叫 Easel 的玩意，看完真有点说不出话。

做号最折磨人的根本不是没灵感，是到处扒热搜、排期、改图、剪片子这一堆杂碎脏活。

它直接把全网热榜吸过来硬对你的账号风格，脚本、日历加几十种物料一条龙怼出来。

我自己跑了两个号的复盘逻辑，发现它能根据数据反馈调整调性，这点我挺服气，越往后跑越像真人写的东西。

不过我坚持提醒一句，这帮平台风控有多恶心大家心里有数，尤其是小红书抓自动化抓得极狠。

I stopped letting Opus make every small decision in my agents. Jev makes them now.

My Opus bill dropped ~500% on the same tasks, same results.

Here's what Jev handles:

- which files and notes to load before Opus sees anything
- which effort level each task actually needs
- what to do when a tool fails
- which tests to run, and when to stop

Opus only gets called for the hard reasoning.

Every decision is a typed result the host checks before it runs.

text:
i gave Jev Bot $50 and told it "pay for yourself or you die"

18 hours later it's holding $8,220

and it's still alive

autonomous trading agent on the platform

no code on my end, it runs on its own cloud machine, trades while my laptop's shut

every 12 minutes it:

> scans every open market before the crowd catches on
> reads the signal against what the posted odds still assume
> computes a threshold before it commits
> sizes the position, kelly criterion, max 4% bankroll
> executes
> pays its own hosting cost from profits

if the balance hits $0, the bot dies

it dipped to $6 at hour five, then stopped touching anything where the signal and the odds still disagreed

so it learned to survive

setup took one evening: build it, run one trade in front of it, schedule it, connect a wallet

no VPS. no API keys. no code to maintain

$50 → $8,220 in 18 hours

how much do you think it has by next week?

答案是：谁都没错。美元流动性多数时候只是背景板，资产定价的主角还是增长、通胀和盈利；只有当融资受阻、中介缩表、被动抛售三者互相强化，流动性才会成为主要矛盾。

这期视频用一套完整的方法论讲清楚：
✅ 美元流动性的四层框架：货币层、离岸层、信用层、金融市场层——每层回答什么问题、历史上怎么出过事（2019 回购、2023 硅谷银行、欧债、英国 LDI、瑞信、2024 日元套息平仓）
✅ 指标怎么看：价格类领先、数量类辅助、央行工具是尾部确认
✅ 四个阶段怎么应对：局部承压 → 跨层传导 → 现金为王 → 修复确认
✅ 最关键的一步：怎么判断此刻是哪种定价力量在主导——看美股下跌时，美债、黄金、美元怎么走

让 AI 做 PPT，出来的多半是套模板，一页堆满要点，自己都不好意思拿去讲。

StackBlitz 开源的 Bolt Slides 换了个做法，每一页幻灯片都是一个能交互的网页，整套做完分享出去就是一个链接。

示例是 26 页，图表、数字滚动、3D 地球、代码窗口、定价表都有，主题里写好了 9 种风格方向，改一个主色整套跟着变。

GitHub：https://t.co/iqOUQ6VdaE

仓库里自带一份 Skill，Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 都能用，一句话说清讲给谁、讲什么，就能出一整套能直接上台的演示。

演讲者模式在另一个标签页打开，带计时、下一页预览和备注，跟观众看的那页同步翻。

我挺喜欢批注这个细节，在电脑上圈住一个数字，换到手机上看，圈还在那个数字上，不会因为排版变了就错位。

text:
生物科技牛市来了！再不看这 17 只医疗股，你将踏空下一个十年：

1. 礼来 $LLY
减肥药绝对王者，GLP-1 全球第一梯队。除了糖尿病和减肥，下一代口服药、心血管、阿尔茨海默症管线都在推进，成长故事还没讲完。

2. 诺和诺德 $NVO
GLP-1 另一位霸主。市场担心竞争，但口服减肥药和新一代产品正在路上，全球肥胖市场足够大，它依旧是核心玩家。

3. 辉瑞 $PFE
曾经的新冠药王，现在成了价值洼地。估值便宜、现金流强，还有大量并购储备，一旦新产品兑现，很容易迎来估值修复。

4. 默沙东 $MRK
Keytruda 是全球最赚钱的抗癌药之一，公司正在布局下一代癌症免疫疗法，还有减肥药赛道的新动作。

5. 阿斯利康 $AZN
癌症创新药大赢家，ADC 药物全球领先，产品线覆盖肿瘤、心血管、呼吸系统，是大型药企里增长最快的一批。

6. BioMarin $BMRN
专攻罕见病，别人卷百亿美元市场，它卷没人能做的疾病。现金流稳定，还有基因疗法持续放量。

7. 福泰制药 $VRTX
不仅有囊性纤维化现金牛，今年肾病新药数据惊艳市场，被认为可能打开一个几十亿美元的新市场。

8. 再生元制药 $REGN
AI 制药概念龙头之一，眼科、肿瘤、免疫三条主线齐发力，研发能力一直是华尔街公认顶级。

9. 安进 $AMGN
礼来和诺和诺德最大的挑战者。长效减肥药 MariTide 被不少机构视为 GLP-1 第二阶段的重要变量。

10. 罗氏 $RHHBY
ADC、癌症和减肥药全面布局，研发底蕴非常深，属于容易被忽视的欧洲医药巨头。

11. CRISPR Therapeutics $CRSP
基因编辑真正进入商业化时代，第一款 CRISPR 疗法已经上市，行业从讲故事进入赚钱阶段。

12. Intellia Therapeutics $NTLA
全球领先的体内 CRISPR 编辑公司，不需要体外改造细胞，技术路线想象空间非常大。

13. Beam Therapeutics $BEAM
比 CRISPR 更进一步的 Base Editing 技术，精度更高，被很多人称为下一代基因编辑平台。

14. Revolution Medicines $RVMD
癌症 KRAS 靶点明星公司，这条赛道过去被认为不可攻克，现在不断有突破，属于高弹性创新药代表。

15. Scholar Rock $SRRK
GLP-1 最大痛点就是掉肌肉，它研发的是保肌肉疗法，被认为是减肥药产业链里的黑马。

16. Maze Therapeutics $MAZE
肾病创新药新贵，最近同赛道临床成功直接带飞整个板块，不少机构认为还有很大的重估空间。

17. 莫德纳 $MRNA  
今年医疗板块最有故事的反转股，没有之一。  过去大家觉得 Moderna 只有新冠疫苗，疫情结束公司就没增长了。但现在市场重新定价的是它的 mRNA 癌症疫苗。

你重仓了几只？

text:
this is pure treasure: 20 open-source JEV combos you can plug into real products.

JEV gives you 3 primitives: Choice, Score and Noul. it makes the judgment, code enforces the rules, and another tool executes the work.

ROUTE THE WORK

 1.⁠ ⁠JEV × Hermes Agent
   route decisions into autonomous agent workflows.

⁠ https://t.co/D6udyyWoDq ⁠

 2.⁠ ⁠JEV × LangGraph
   use JEV as a decision layer inside graph-based agent flows.

⁠ https://t.co/mTmgIE2ZzB ⁠

 3.⁠ ⁠JEV × MCP SDK
   let JEV decide which tool or action should run next.

⁠ https://t.co/410qS3HBY4 ⁠

 4.⁠ ⁠JEV × Temporal
   use JEV decisions inside durable workflows.

⁠ https://t.co/KiBM5twlJw ⁠

 5.⁠ ⁠JEV × E2B
   combine narrow decisions with sandboxed code execution.

⁠ https://t.co/hATdEoHVQq ⁠

FIND THE EVIDENCE

 6.⁠ ⁠JEV × Meilisearch
   retrieve relevant context before making a decision.

⁠ https://t.co/pCc9iqMkAG ⁠

 7.⁠ ⁠JEV × Qdrant
   score decisions against vector-retrieved evidence.

⁠ https://t.co/mE99OI4drc ⁠

 8.⁠ ⁠JEV × Docling
   turn documents into structured context for JEV.

⁠ https://t.co/tuMHzAiYtU ⁠

 9.⁠ ⁠JEV × Graphiti
   use graph memory to give JEV better context.

⁠ https://t.co/RKvtaaeZus ⁠

10.⁠ ⁠JEV × LlamaIndex
    connect retrieval pipelines directly to the decision layer.

⁠ https://t.co/p8OakXtEKD ⁠

VERIFY THE RESULT

11.⁠ ⁠JEV × Langfuse
    trace and inspect decisions in production.

⁠ https://t.co/myfxAVFrLl ⁠

12.⁠ ⁠JEV × Promptfoo
    test JEV decisions against evals and failure cases.

⁠ https://t.co/sGCAeJKU0h ⁠

13.⁠ ⁠JEV × Semgrep
    judge findings, then let code enforce security rules.

⁠ https://t.co/INgdNlpgOv ⁠

14.⁠ ⁠JEV × Sentry
    route errors into the right recovery path.

⁠ https://t.co/WydOSioGsp ⁠

text:
Codex 6 必装 Product Hunt 插件，直接让你当老板

我现在很多赚钱想法，都是这样来的，现在公司朋友帮我管着，收益6位数，这个办法我认为最少价值10万

不是坐着硬想项目，也不是问 AI “最近有什么风口”，多总结分析例子很关键，直接让 Codex 6 去 Product Hunt 找

直接丢这段提示词，这是我优化过的，你可以直接用：

「使用 Product Hunt 插件，分析最近 30 天发布或热度明显上升的 AI 产品，重点关注 AI Agent、效率工具、内容创作、开发者工具、销售自动化。筛选 20 个值得研究的产品，分析它们解决的核心问题、目标用户、收费方式、用户为什么愿意付费、评论区高频抱怨、竞品缺陷和仍未被满足的需求。然后从中筛出 5 个适合个人开发者切入的赚钱机会，每个机会输出：真实用户痛点、现有竞品、竞品缺陷、差异化切入点、最小 MVP、建议定价、第一批用户获取渠道、7 天验证方案。不要给泛泛的创业建议，只选择已经有真实付费需求、但现有方案明显不够好的机会。最后按：机会｜用户｜痛点｜竞品｜市场空白｜MVP｜定价｜获客｜验证方法 输出」

直接找出了最近 30 天增长快、已经有人付钱的产品，再看用户还在骂什么、竞品哪里没做好、有没有个人开发者能切进去的空白

先找已经赚钱的需求 → 再找没解决好的问题 → 最后切一个更便宜、更简单的小市场

千问别凭空想项目，这个方法我用了半年多，很靠谱

最离谱的是黏土动画，直接调用 Blender，把完整动画做出来，效果比Codex 6 好 10倍

让它一次生成 500 种健身器材，还顺手做出完整的健身房建模器。从单个器材、材质调整，到整个空间的布局设计，一句话就能自动完成，效率提高 90 %

text:
做美股连这10个网站都不知道，先别急着拿真金白银进场交学费！

1、TradingView：看K线和技术面非常顺手，支持多周期图表、技术指标、选股器、热力图以及价格提醒，做趋势跟踪和关键价位监控效率很高。
https://t.co/0J0oBWPS4H

2、SEC EDGAR：美国证监会官方披露系统，10-K、10-Q、8-K、Form 4等公司文件都能直接查。研究一家公司，与其只看别人总结，不如学会回到原始公告。
https://t.co/kWKQeyOJFX

3、TIKR：偏基本面深度研究，财务三表、估值倍数、分析师一致预期、电话会记录、机构持仓和全球选股器都能查，特别适合做公司和同行横向对比。
https://t.co/VXv8sjZXST

4、Quartr：财报季非常好用，可以集中查看公司电话会、历史文字稿、投资者演示材料和公告，还能搜索管理层过去说过什么，研究公司预期变化很方便。
https://t.co/tukC6ky2kH

5、CME FedWatch：专门观察市场对美联储加息、降息以及维持利率不变的预期。做美股一定要知道市场当前到底在交易怎样的利率路径。
https://t.co/hjdBcXuL1k

6、Cboe：想研究VIX和美股期权，这个网站值得常看。VIX、期权成交量、Put/Call Ratio以及波动率相关数据都能找到，适合辅助观察市场风险偏好。
https://t.co/QkUl1VizGq

7、WhaleWisdom：专门追踪机构13F持仓，可以查看基金历史持仓、增减仓以及多家机构的共同持仓，研究“聪明钱”在配置什么很方便，不过13F存在披露时滞。
https://t.co/CjXXARvbJP

text:
holy sh*t . Jev Founder, Diogo Almeida just released a 11-page PDF whole Jev + AI agents loop

this is a 9-step blueprint on how to run your LLM through agents without paying frontier prices for every fork they hit:

step 1 → split the loop into three kinds of work: generation stays with the LLM, exact rules like action and spend caps stay in code, every fork in between becomes a typed question to Jev

step 2 → start every job with one Noul: is this in scope, or does it need a human before anything runs

step 3 → dispatch with a Choice: research, write or review. act only at confidence 0.85+, everything below goes to review

step 4 → call the LLM only where text has to be written: planning the task and filling tool arguments, nothing else

step 5 → gate every tool call before it runs: allow, confirm or block, plus a destructive check in the same round trip

step 6 → score what comes back: drop, summary or keep. nothing gets rewritten, so nothing is lost to a bad paraphrase

step 7 → close with two checks: Jev says the goal is met above 0.8, then code proves the file actually exists

step 8 → send the risky tail to a human: irreversible, touches money or visible outside the company gets a person whatever the confidence

step 9 → move one fork first and track three numbers for a week: cost per completed task, time per completed task, how often escalation fired and whether it was right

text:
《规划一个产品要依次回答的 8 个问题》

产品规划是产品成败最重要的问题。它不是一门统一的学科，而是几套互相衔接的框架，分别回答不同的问题。

1. 用户到底要完成什么事：Jobs to Be Done

核心：用户不是在买产品，而是"雇"一个东西去完成一件事。你的竞争对手，是用户为了这件事可能去雇的所有东西，不只是同类产品。

读物：Clayton Christensen《Competing Against Luck》；Bob Moesta《Demand-Side Sales 101》。

2. 凭什么选你：定位

核心：April Dunford 的定位五步：用户不用你的话会怎么做（竞争替代品）；
你有哪些它们没有的东西；
这些东西给用户带来什么价值；
谁最在乎这个价值；
把自己放进哪个品类，用户才一下子就懂。
定位不是一句口号，是从"替代品"一步步推出来的。

读物：April Dunford《Obviously Awesome》，最实用，建议第一本读。Ries 和 Trout 的《Positioning》是它的源头。

3. 先打哪一小块：滩头市场

核心：新产品先占领一个足够小、彼此会互相推荐、痛点一致的细分市场，站稳之后再扩到相邻市场。窄是策略，不是缺陷。

读物：Geoffrey Moore《Crossing the Chasm》，重点读滩头市场那几章。

4. 用户为什么会回来：核心动作、自然频率和习惯

核心动作：用户在产品里最有价值的那个重复动作，所有功能都应该围绕它。

自然频率：用户"本来就"多久需要一次这个价值。产品的频率不能硬拉，只能贴合，比如报税是一年一次，聊天是一天几十次。

Aha 时刻：用户第一次真正感受到价值的瞬间，产品要让新用户尽快走到这一步。

习惯模型（Nir Eyal）：触发 → 行动 → 不确定的奖励 → 投入。每周邮件是触发；"这周有没有新对手"是不确定的奖励；关注列表越积越长是投入。

读物：Reforge 创始人 Brian Balfour、Casey Winters 关于留存和"natural frequency"的文章；Nir Eyal《Hooked》，读的时候要带点批判。

5. 先留存，后获客：产品市场契合

核心：留存曲线不走平之前，花钱获客等于往漏桶里倒水。验证产品市场契合，常用 Sean Ellis 的问题："如果不能再用这个产品，你会有多失望？"回答"非常失望"的比例达到 40% 左右，才算有了契合。

读物：Marc Andreessen《The only thing that matters》，一篇短博客；First Round Review 上 Superhuman 的 Rahul Vohra 写的产品市场契合方法；Paul Graham《Do Things That Don't Scale》。

6. 怎么获客：增长循环和"四个契合"

增长循环：把获客想成一个闭环，而不是一个漏斗。用户的行为产生内容或邀请，内容和邀请再带来新用户。

四个契合（Brian Balfour）：市场和产品、产品和渠道、渠道和商业模式、商业模式和市场，这四对必须同时匹配。比如每月 $10 的产品，养不起销售团队这种渠道。

渠道选择：Gabriel Weinberg 和 Justin Mares 的《Traction》列了 19 种渠道和一套"靶心"筛选法：先广泛测试，再集中到一两个渠道上。

读物：Balfour 的"Four Fits"系列文章，免费；Reforge 的《Growth Loops are the New Funnels》。

7. 怎么收钱：先定价，再做产品

核心：在做产品之前先测付费意愿，围绕用户愿意付钱的那部分来设计功能，而不是做完再想怎么收费。

读物：Madhavan Ramanujam《Monetizing Innovation》。

8. 怎么验证：别问用户想要什么

核心：问用户"你会不会用、会不会买"，得到的都是客气话。要问他们过去实际做过什么、花过什么钱、怎么解决这个问题的。

读物：Rob Fitzpatrick《The Mom Test》，很薄，建议第二本读。

9. 怎么聚焦：学会说不
精益创业：用最小代价验证最大的假设（Eric Ries《The Lean Startup》）。

Shape Up：先定"这个问题值得花多少时间"，再在这个预算里设计方案（Basecamp 的 Ryan Singer，全书免费公开）。

独立开发者视角：Rob Walling《The SaaS Playbook》；Arvid Kahl《The Embedded Entrepreneur》，讲先找到一个社群，再从里面长出产品。

最后才是功能清单：每个功能都要回答它服务于第 4 步还是第 6 步，答不出来就不做。

OpusNet created by Claude watched four markets at the same time. BTC. ETH. SOL. ADA. All on Binance. All with order flow running underneath.

While you pick one chart and stare at it for hours, this terminal reads the delta on all four and trades whichever one moves first.

The final frame tells the story. BTC long at +$180. SOL short at +$436. ADA long at +$725. ETH short running live with a stop at 2,707 and target at 2,693. All four screens printing at once.

$200 to $5,421 is 27x in two days. Run it for a week and the math breaks your calculator.

text:
A man spends 50 years teaching at MIT.

He knows his time is running out.

So he records one last lecture — everything he knows, distilled into a single hour.

He died 5 months later.

This is that lecture.

The most important hour you'll watch this week.👇

Bookmark it https://t.co/XTZTwQRDgh

quotedTweet.text:
An MIT professor gives a student $5 and says: send any amount to a stranger in this room. Whatever you send triples. The stranger decides how much comes back.

Rational answer: send nothing. You lose every dollar you trust.

Most students send almost everything. Most strangers return more than half. The math says keep it. The room says otherwise.

Then the professor runs a different game. Same cash. Same room. One student splits. The other can only accept. No rejection. No consequences.

The offers collapse. Not to zero. But enough to see the line between generosity and strategy.

One year a student got Swiss chocolate instead of cash. She was lactose intolerant. Gave away 100%. The professor noted it. The class laughed. Nobody noticed the point.

She had zero cost of generosity. The moment giving costs nothing, everyone is generous. The moment real money hits the table, the room divides into the same two groups every semester. People who send first. People who wait.

Labor, capital, arbitrage, insurance. Four ways to make money. All four require the same opening move.

You send value before you see a return. A paycheck after the work. A deposit before the interest. A bet before the edge. A premium before the claim.

The lecture is free. MIT filmed it years ago. The game runs every semester. The split barely changes. 

Sending first is free. Knowing if it comes back is the part that costs something.

result.text:
An MIT professor gives a student $5 and says: send any amount to a stranger in this room. Whatever you send triples. The stranger decides how much comes back.

Rational answer: send nothing. You lose every dollar you trust.

Most students send almost everything. Most strangers return more than half. The math says keep it. The room says otherwise.

Then the professor runs a different game. Same cash. Same room. One student splits. The other can only accept. No rejection. No consequences.

The offers collapse. Not to zero. But enough to see the line between generosity and strategy.

One year a student got Swiss chocolate instead of cash. She was lactose intolerant. Gave away 100%. The professor noted it. The class laughed. Nobody noticed the point.

She had zero cost of generosity. The moment giving costs nothing, everyone is generous. The moment real money hits the table, the room divides into the same two groups every semester. People who send first. People who wait.

Labor, capital, arbitrage, insurance. Four ways to make money. All four require the same opening move.

You send value before you see a return. A paycheck after the work. A deposit before the interest. A bet before the edge. A premium before the claim.

The lecture is free. MIT filmed it years ago. The game runs every semester. The split barely changes. 

Sending first is free. Knowing if it comes back is the part that costs something.

text:
So I know Cognition doesn’t care about Little Ole’ Me, and this is just my story, so take it with a grain of salt, but here’s why I don’t think all these crazy scaling revenue numbers by coding agents are going to stick:

We’ve been happy Devin users for a while. Really like the product, and like the company. Still do! This isn’t shade at Cognition, and I’m not upset with them, just a sample of why I worry about the competitive landscape for these cos. 

Anyway, our usage grew to >$100k run rate or so. I think one or two of our users even received an email congratulating them for being Top 200 users of Devin. 

As usage grew, we added more capabilities and needed a BAA (layman’s terms: an agreement that says they are HIPAA compliant). This required an Enterprise contract (why a piece of paper requires extra money is a topic for another discussion, but it’s very normal…) so we started talking to their sales team. 

Basically, we were going to ~1.5x our spend in order to get the BAA. Honestly, that was fine with us. We like Devin!

Our only request was to pay quarterly (already a big concession from our existing monthly payments, given our relatively small size). They declined, unless we committed to EVEN MORE usage. 

Before responding, I decided to see how difficult it would be to set up Hermes to do the equivalent work as Devin, and to see what the costs were. I’d host it in our infrastructure and only use providers we already have a BAA with. 

Two days. 

That’s it. It’s functionally 100% equivalent. Maybe slightly better in some ways, slightly worse in others. We spend a little bit of time futzing with it, but we did that with Devin, too. 

The cost is roughly 25% of Devin. 

So, two days for $100k or so per year savings. All because they didn’t want us to pay quarterly. 

At some point, other companies are going to catch onto this, too. So congrats on this milestone, but keep finding more ways to provide value and keep customers happy. It’s hard to compete.

result.text:
So I know Cognition doesn’t care about Little Ole’ Me, and this is just my story, so take it with a grain of salt, but here’s why I don’t think all these crazy scaling revenue numbers by coding agents are going to stick:

We’ve been happy Devin users for a while. Really like the product, and like the company. Still do! This isn’t shade at Cognition, and I’m not upset with them, just a sample of why I worry about the competitive landscape for these cos. 

Anyway, our usage grew to >$100k run rate or so. I think one or two of our users even received an email congratulating them for being Top 200 users of Devin. 

As usage grew, we added more capabilities and needed a BAA (layman’s terms: an agreement that says they are HIPAA compliant). This required an Enterprise contract (why a piece of paper requires extra money is a topic for another discussion, but it’s very normal…) so we started talking to their sales team. 

Basically, we were going to ~1.5x our spend in order to get the BAA. Honestly, that was fine with us. We like Devin!

Our only request was to pay quarterly (already a big concession from our existing monthly payments, given our relatively small size). They declined, unless we committed to EVEN MORE usage. 

Before responding, I decided to see how difficult it would be to set up Hermes to do the equivalent work as Devin, and to see what the costs were. I’d host it in our infrastructure and only use providers we already have a BAA with. 

Two days. 

That’s it. It’s functionally 100% equivalent. Maybe slightly better in some ways, slightly worse in others. We spend a little bit of time futzing with it, but we did that with Devin, too. 

The cost is roughly 25% of Devin. 

So, two days for $100k or so per year savings. All because they didn’t want us to pay quarterly. 

At some point, other companies are going to catch onto this, too. So congrats on this milestone, but keep finding more ways to provide value and keep customers happy. It’s hard to compete.

我只投了89美元，之后再也没有追加资金。

6个Grok机器人，在一个横盘躺平10小时的Cate猫币，赚到55698.17美元。

8月一开始放进去89美元。
10号跟Astra对局开启，又加了1000美元进去。
今早六点，账户资金到55698.17美元。

从最开始到现在，我从来没有发过任何交易截图出去？

上一轮收盘赚11366.61美元，20小时收益25.64%。

机器人交易的Cate猫币，中间有10小时几乎没行情。

→那10小时市值就在79M到85M来回震荡，每一次波动都不足3%。
→震荡期间完成9笔日间交易，赚1475.74美元。
→晚上继续做了8笔交易，盈利6274.26美元，机器人和规则没变。
→最漂亮的一笔，90.5M买入，30分钟后106.7M卖出，赚2055.88美元。
→有四次机器人追涨进场，全部亏钱，合计亏717.30美元。
→币没动静的时候，后台同时跑8笔预测投注，赚了3616.61美元。
→其中一笔押Anthropic今年不会IPO，短短3小时价格从45.5c涨到96.8c。

币种交易单笔风险5878美元。

预测投注风险只有756美元，却拿下当天三分之一的收益。

这段时间币本身涨幅只有13.66%。
机器人操作拿到25.64%的收益。

我写好了指南交给6个Grok机器人运行，同一时间只开一个仓位。

分工：1个负责扫市场，1个算仓位大小，1个买入，1个记录侧投注，1个专门管住不去追涨。

这套策略，89美元本金能跑，资金涨到55000美元也没问题。

市面上不少信号群每月收400美元，亏钱的信号直接删掉，只放盈利记录。

我保留了4笔亏损订单在图表上，整套方案全部免费放在下文：提示词、仓位规则、各个机器人的断点参数全都有。

抓紧收藏，不然很快就被信息流埋掉了。

https://t.co/LWbSvnaPvm

要是十天前你也投入89美元，你昨晚能安心睡觉吗？

This doc dropped on a private Telegram for 2 seconds before getting nuked. Someone screenshotted it. Now it's everywhere.

Jim Simons' inner circle called it "the only sheet you need before entering any position." Citadel's risk desk ran these exact numbers before every trade that built their $60B book.

"Risk, Return & Position Sizing." Trading & Quantitative Finance Series. Working Note No. 07. The mathematical cheat sheet that separates traders who print from traders who get rekt - and it fits on one page.

No more gambling. No more guessing entries. Pure math.

Here's the edge most traders never learn.

45% win rate. 2:1 risk-reward. Most retail traders would fade that setup instantly - too many losses. The document runs the expected value: +35% per trade. Over 100 trades that's 35% return on initial capital. The math doesn't care about your emotions. It only cares about edge.

Position sizing. $10,000 account. Risk 1% per trade - $100. Stop loss 2%, point value $1 per move. Position size: 50 units. Fixed. Every time. No FOMO sizing, no revenge trading, no doubling down after a red week. The document calls it the fixed fractional approach. Quants at Two Sigma call it survival.

Risk of Ruin - the calculation nobody talks about. Same 45% win rate, 2:1 reward-to-risk, 200 trades. Probability of blowing the entire account: 0.06%. Not zero. But 0.06%. That's the number that separates professionals from degenerates. Citadel traders know their RoR before they know their entry price.

50/200 MA crossover. RSI. MACD. Bollinger Bands. ATR for stop placement. Every indicator a prop desk runs daily - their formulas, their exact definitions, one table.

Stop guessing. Start calculating.

Watch the moment [Table: Trade Example]

Over 100 trades: expected return 35% on initial capital.

The only stat sheet you need open before market hours.

text:
做 A 股短线复盘的朋友，大概率踩过不少“AI 炒股”工具的坑：很多项目最大的毛病是让大模型直接去“猜”行情、算涨跌，幻觉一多，数据根本不敢用。

最近在 GitHub 看到一个架构思路非常清醒的开源项目：vibe-astock。

它把“算数据”和“写研判”拆得特别干净：

硬指标纯计算直出：涨停池、连板梯队、赚钱效应、晋级率、梯队断层、情绪周期这些关键数据，全部由本地确定性代码计算，不经过大模型，杜绝 AI 乱编数字。

AI 只当材料整理员：大模型只负责拿着算好的证据链，把盘面、题材变化和龙虎榜串成结构化的复盘报告，而且带引用核验，哪句话对应哪个数据一目了然。

白嫖订阅，省 Token 费：支持直接复用本机 Claude CLI 或 Codex 订阅，不用额外掏 API Key 钱；想用 DeepSeek 或国内模型的也预留了接口。

功能很克制：七个模块覆盖盯盘、昨日梯队承接、首板分析、个股多空辩论（分别列正反论据，不给任何买卖点建议）和交易台账，全部跑在本地网页端。

对做短线的人来说，复盘的核心是建立稳定的观察坐标，而不是听 AI 算命。工具负责把繁琐的数据扒下来算好，人来做最后决策，这种界限感才是真正能落地的辅助工具。习惯自己盯盘复盘的同学可以跑一个试试。

https://t.co/5Ih8ttmhsK

text:
this paper is f*cking brilliant
  
a computer science paper builds the Digital Apprentice framework to grant AI agents earned autonomy  
  
the result: per-skill authorization gates and inference-time quality control expand agent authority only when backed by empirical proof  
  
the crazy part is how earned autonomy replaces blanket agent permissions  
  
agents start at low-autonomy tiers, learn tacit expert methodology, and require explicit human authorization to graduate to high-risk tasks  
  
most developers either grant full autonomous control or restrict agents to stateless copilot prompts  
  
this framework establishes a progressive governance control plane for safe AI delegation

text:
过去优化 harness 是纯人肉活，Agent 工程师翻执行轨迹、找失败模式、然后再手工翻译成代码改动。慢，而且难规模化。

现在 NVIDIA 在这篇研究中把这件事自动化了，他们做了一个名SoL-Pi 把这个流程自动化，思路是 RSI 。

核心思路就是一个研究 AI 观察另一个跑基础 Pi 的 agent 的执行轨迹，然后再提出候选改动，在准备好的环境里实现、复查、测试；

并且最后的结果中，还把编码 agent 的 token 流量砍掉 49%，API 成本降 1/3。

不过这种流量和成本的下降是以6%的能力下降换来的。

arxiv：https://t.co/BrfDubhDkg

Codex 需要验证手机号，我们该怎么办？

之前我给一个朋友装了 Codex 桌面版，结果卡在了手机号验证这里。

这个验证还是必选项，但大陆手机号收不到验证码，他手上又没有能用的国际手机号，所以 Codex 虽然装好了，最后一直没用上。

昨天我看到一个插件，可以直接使用你网页版 ChatGPT 已经登录好的账号信息，亲测有效，所以分享一下。

这个方法的原理是：

你的 Chrome 浏览器里面，ChatGPT 是可以使用邮箱登录的。

插件做的事情，就是把你浏览器里这份“已经登录成功的身份信息”导出来，生成一个 auth.json 文件，然后再把这个文件放进 Codex 的指定文件夹。

Codex 看到这份文件以后，就知道：哦，这个账号已经登录过了，于是可以直接读取这份登录状态。

插件是这个：

codex-auth-helper（Codex 认证助手）

仓库：

https://t.co/yio1jakR2o

────────────────────────

1/ 先把插件下载下来

打开上面的 GitHub 地址，进去以后，找到绿色的 Code

点开以后选择 Download ZIP，下载后解压。

这里注意不要直接选最外层的文件夹。

打开解压出来的文件夹以后，里面还有一个：extension

我们需要的是这个文件夹。

如何判断自己有没有选对：

打开 extension 以后，你应该能看到类似：

manifest.json、icons、popup 等这些文件。

看到 manifest.json 基本就说明找对了。

────────────────────────

2/ 把插件装进 Chrome

打开 Chrome，直接在地址栏输入 ：

chrome://extensions/

然后回车。

进去以后：

① 打开右上角的 「开发者模式」

② 点击左上角 「加载已解压的扩展程序」

③ 选择刚才找到的 extension 文件夹

加载成功以后，你的 Chrome 里面就会多出一个：

Codex 认证助手

建议顺手点一下 Chrome 右上角的拼图图标，把它固定到浏览器工具栏。

────────────────────────

3/ 把自己的登录信息导出来

接下来先打开：https://t.co/dED8eBc2XW

确认你的 ChatGPT 已经正常登录。

然后点击浏览器右上角刚才安装好的 Codex 认证助手。

如果插件能够正常识别你的账号，你会看到自己的账号、套餐以及登录凭证剩余有效时间等信息。

然后点击里面生成 / 保存 auth.json 的按钮。

浏览器会下载一个文件：auth.json

这个文件非常重要。

你可以把它理解成 Codex 用来识别你登录身份的文件。

所以不要把这个文件发给别人，也不要上传到网盘、群聊或者任何公开的地方。

────────────────────────

4/ 把 auth.json 放进 Codex 文件夹

这一步很多不熟悉电脑的人可能会懵，所以我详细说一下。

Windows 用户按：Win + R

然后输入：%USERPROFILE%\.codex\   回车。

把刚才下载的：auth.json  直接放进这个文件夹。

最后应该是：%USERPROFILE%\.codex\auth.json

如果里面本来已经有一个 auth.json，就用新下载的覆盖掉。

Mac 用户

打开 Finder，顶部菜单选择：

前往 → 前往文件夹

或者直接按：Command + Shift + G

输入：~/.codex/  回车。

然后把刚才下载的：auth.json  放进去。

最后的位置就是：~/.codex/auth.json

如果原来已经有一个，就直接覆盖。

────────────────────────

5/ 重新打开 Codex

文件放好以后，彻底退出 Codex 桌面端。（要确保 Codex 已经完全退出，后台也没有继续运行。）

然后重新打开 Codex。

如果前面的步骤都正确，Codex 就会读取刚才放进去的 auth.json。

最后还有一点：

这个 auth.json 不是永久有效的，插件里面会显示剩余有效时间。

如果失效了，重新打开已经登录 ChatGPT 的 Chrome：

点插件 → 再生成一次 auth.json → 覆盖掉原来的文件。

然后重启 Codex 就会重新生效。

text:
贝莱德这篇论文，把 AI × Crypto 最重要的一条钱路讲明白了：以后机器会自己花钱（都是知识）

AI Agent 真正跑起来以后，它每天都要买数据、调用 API、租 GPU、订软件，而且很多交易可能只有几美分，却要求 7×24 小时自动完成。

信用卡、ACH 这些支付系统本来是围绕“人”设计的，Agent 需要一套机器可以直接调用、即时结算、金额可以小到几分钱的金融系统。

贝莱德给出的答案就是稳定币 + 区块链。

2025 年过滤掉交易所内部转账、机器人等噪音后，稳定币交易量已经达到 11.2 万亿美元，2020—2025 年复合增速 80%，同期 ACH 只有约 8.5%。

更重要的是，Agent 通过 x402 买 API、用稳定币付款，每增加一次机器交易，都可能继续传导成区块空间、验证和结算需求，最后碰到 ETH 这类公链原生资产。

但我觉得贝莱德这篇最有意思的地方，其实是后半段：

算力可能会直接变成一种金融资产。

2025—2030 年 AI 基础设施累计资本开支可能超过 5 万亿美元，AWS、微软 Intelligent Cloud 和 Google Cloud 到 2030 年收入合计预计约 1.1 万亿美元。

到那时候，AI 推理预计会吃掉全球数据中心约 43% 的电力需求。

以后 GPU 算力使用权完全可能被标准化、代币化，做成可以交易、融资、抵押甚至对冲的资产，Agent 自己比价格、延迟和芯片型号，然后自动买算力、自动付款。

这条链一旦跑通，Crypto 面对的用户就不只是一群人在交易资产，而是海量 AI Agent 全天候买数据、买算力、做支付、做结算。

稳定币变成机器的现金，公链变成机器的结算层，Tokenized RWA 是机器可以调用的资产，算力甚至可能成为下一类链上商品。

贝莱德已经开始按这个框架重新看数字资产了。

🔥GitHub 绝对是个被严重低估的搞钱宝藏库。 只要你执行力够强，里面到处都是现成的赚钱💰路子

之前和大家分享过这个核心逻辑：直接去 GitHub 进货，把开源的优质项目搬运、包装，再卖给特定的人群

分享几个方向👇

1. AI 工具变现：把 GPT-SoVITS 打包成“声音克隆一键安装包”，精准卖给做数字人或配音的自媒体新手

2. 外贸刚需出海：把 pyvideotrans 这种视频翻译神器做好环境配置，直接卖给急需做跨境短视频获客的外贸小白

3. 自动化提效脚本：去搜几个小红书或抖音的无水印批量下载脚本，打包解决同行运营工具人的素材抓取痛点

4. 短视频量产工具：把 MoneyPrinterV2 做好部署，包装成“输入一句话、3秒量产视频”的脚本神器，卖给需要批量起号的 TikTok 玩家或本地引流商家。

5. 企业级 AI 落地：把 Dify 包装成“免编程、一键导入文档的 AI 智能客服”，去线下帮传统的本地中小企业做定制，轻松收一笔服务费。

6. 自动化工作流：把 n8n 调好模板，包装成“电商数据自动同步、全网自动发帖机器人”，卖给跨境独立站长或电商卖家。

赚钱的本质就是信息差。

你以为的常识，往往是别人的壁垒

以上。

text:
不知道你和我是否有一样的疑问：公司要怎样用 AI 才能回本？为什么 AI 看似提效，但是团队整体产出没有增多？

这是我这两周在深入思考的问题，先说结论，后面配合上我引用的案例
1. 看平均情况，AI Token支出回本其实不难
2. 很多人用 AI 优化的task，看似提效，却不是整件事情的卡点
3. AI 优化的效能还是被以人为中心的旧流程卡死，不够 AI native。企业需要改革，AI新流程可以激发更好的创造力和效率

Ramp 用 7 万多家美国企业的支出数据做统计，7 月中位数公司每个员工每月只花 11.95 美元 [1]。美国雇主为一个员工付出的综合成本是每小时 49.46 美元，按全职工时折下来每月 8,500 美元左右 [2]。AI 只要让这个人每周多产出 30分钟，这笔钱就回本了

单个任务上的提升也是实打实的。宝洁做过一个 776 人的实验，一个人带着 AI 做出来的产品方案，质量追平了没有 AI 的两人小组 [3]

那为什么很多公司上了 AI，整体却没快多少？

我做推理优化，第一件事是先看请求慢在哪。瓶颈不在的地方，优化得再好也没用。公司用 AI 是一个道理

举个假设的例子（防杠，真实项目比这复杂很多）：一个需求从提出到上线要 10 天，写代码 2 天，剩下 8 天在 review、对齐、排期、等审批，或者推理环境崩掉，导致部分项目重做。AI 把写代码压到半天，总时间从 10 天变成 8.5 天

代码快了 4 倍，整件事只省了 15%

今年有个 515 家创业公司的实验 [4]。所有公司拿到同样的 AI 额度、模型和技术培训，唯一的区别是案例课：随机一半看的是别的公司怎么围绕 AI 重排工作，另一半看的是普通创业案例。结果前一半的整体收入是后一半的 1.9 倍

工具一模一样，最大的区别在于

所以很多公司在考核 AI 使用率，我觉得考核错了。用得多不等于做得快

作为 manager 我的建议：先删流程，再简化，最后才上 AI

你们公司用上 AI 之后，哪个环节真的变快了，哪个一点没变？

text:
Brilliant paper from CMU.

If you use Jev/LLM-as-judge, this one is for you.

(bookmark it)

We use LLMs to generate answers, then use another LLM to judge them.

But many evaluations only need a bounded decision.

- Was the answer grounded?
- Did it follow the instruction?
- Which response was better?

This Carnegie Mellon University paper tests whether Jev can make these decisions cheaply, then identifies the cases that need a stronger judge.

The results reveal Jev’s real edge.

→ Jev works well on focused judgments

On ordinary response preferences, evidence-grounded factuality, and final-answer checks, Jev remained within three percentage points of the strongest judge tested.

→ The cost difference is substantial

On the paper’s matched workload, Jev cost only 0.36 percent of the strongest comparator’s fee.

This makes it practical to evaluate more agent responses, across more criteria, without scaling the evaluation bill at the same rate.

→ Confidence becomes a routing mechanism

Jev returns a decision and label probabilities.

When confidence is high, accept its decision. When confidence is low, escalate the case to a stronger LLM.

A frozen version of this cascade retained about 99 percent of GPT-6’s accuracy while using roughly 57 percent of its fee.

→ Jev still has a clear boundary

It fell behind when evaluation required checking complex derivations or resisting an elaborately written wrong answer.

It also struggled with factuality judgments when no reference evidence was provided. In those cases, confidence did not reliably expose the errors.

So the paper is not arguing that Jev should replace every LLM judge.

It presents a more useful architecture.

Code handles exact rules. Jev handles focused semantic judgments. Stronger models or humans handle uncertain and reasoning-heavy cases.

That is also the idea behind the workflow I built.

The agent generates an answer. Jev judges bounded claims against the supplied evidence. Uncertain cases move to review. Opik records the traces, scores, and experiment results.

The paper explains why this architecture works.

My article shows how to build it.

The full implementation breakdown is quoted below.

语音合成我用的GLM（没有广告合作，单纯是因为自己账号里面还有余额），也可以选其它的TTS，也许比GLM效果更好，让AI帮忙微调一下就行。

text:
龙飞虎是非常有名的语言学家。

教大家一个在 Claude 里面几十个任务一起并行跑的方案：

一般 Claude 里两三个任务并行通常没什么问题，但当几十个任务同时在改一个 Repo 的时候，会有很多 overlap，比如一个 session 测完了提交了，另外一个 session 就白测了，需要重头再来。

我的办法是创建一个 Merge steward，绑定在一个 integration branch，相当于作为一个工程主管，所有的 session 想要 merge，全部交给他，他来看现在是否可以merge，是否会影响其他的 session，作为 merge 的总调度。

这个跟 Subagent 还不太一样，subagent 是做任务拆解，需要传递大量的上下文，反复沟通。而 Merge steward 只负责 merge 一件事情，24h 待命。

目前我并行几十个session运行完全不是问题，瓶颈已经来到了 Mac 端，接下来我继续探索下多 Mac 合作。

微软开源的 SkillOpt 彻底把 Agent 技能优化做成了“神经网络训练”！无需改动底层大模型权重，就能在纯文本空间实现严格、可复现的技能自我进化。🔥

以往 Agent 的 Prompt 或 Skill 要么靠人工反复试错微调，要么靠模型一次性生成或松散的自我修改，极易出现提示词退化。SkillOpt 则将自然语言技能文档视为可训练状态，用优化器严谨迭代：

深度学习训练范式：引入了 Epoch、Batch Size、文本学习率（Textual Learning-Rate Budget）以及拒绝编辑缓冲区，将打分后的执行轨迹转化为有边界的增、删、改操作。

验证门控机制（Validation Gate）：所有针对技能文档的修改，必须在留出的验证集上取得明确的准确率提升才会被采纳，从机制上避免越改越烂。

零额外推理开销：训练收敛后输出的是一个极其紧凑的 best_skill.md 产物（约 300–2,000 tokens），直接挂载到冻结的基座模型即可使用，部署阶段不增加任何额外模型调用。

SkillOpt-Sleep 离线自进化：支持夜间后台静默进化流程（收集会话 → 挖掘任务 → 重放验证 → 固化入库），已原生接入 Claude Code、Codex、Copilot 等本地代码 Agent 工具链。

实测在 GPT-5.5 上，SkillOpt 让纯 Chat 场景准确率直接提升 +23.5，Codex Agentic 循环内提升 +24.8，Claude Code 环境提升 +19.1，且优化后的技能跨模型尺寸迁移效果显著。

项目自带 WebUI 可视化监控面板，支持 OpenAI、Claude、Qwen、MiniMax 等多种后端。做智能体落地或提示词自动调优的开发者非常值得深入研究。

four departments, four pinned versions, and no agent ever reaches into another one's branch

in 60 minutes twelve things exist that did not an hour earlier: the app, the API, the docs, the landing page, the ads, the emails, the help centre, billing, metrics and alerts

three per department, and every one is a file, a page or a rule, not a slide with a plan

payroll for four departments like this is $31,000 a month, the tokens are $450

the agents do the typing, deciding what to build is still on you

120 people at $99, 200 at $299, 29 at $999 make $100,651 a month

the middle plan carries more than half the month, and it is what turns this into $1.2M a year

the hour builds the company, the first customers decide whether it is one

a team out of NASA and MIT built a stripped-down trend and momentum system for gold futures, then tested it strictly out of sample.

the crazy part is the signal itself isn't fancy at all, the real edge comes from turning weak predictability into disciplined sizing, exits, and execution.

We may be witnessing the start of a shift toward precision medicine for mental health.
